title: Square-root logarithmic approximation for metric labeling
area: Approximation algorithms and hardness of approximation
formal: Does a randomized polynomial-time algorithm exist giving an \(O(\sqrt{\log (k+2)})\) approximation for every metric-labeling instance with k labels?
definitions: An instance consists of a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\), nonnegative rational edge weights \(w_{uv}, a\) metric d on \([k]\) supplied by its rational distance matrix, and nonnegative rational assignment costs \(c(v,i)\). A labeling \(f:V\to [k]\) has cost \(\sum_{v} c(v,f(v))+\sum_{uv\in E}w_{uv} d(f(u),f(v))\). The guarantee is \(\operatorname{cost}(f)\le C\sqrt{\log (k+2)}\cdot\)OPT with probability at least \(2/3\) for a universal C. Running time on every random tape is polynomial in the entire binary input length; k is part of the input. No restriction on the metric or graph is promised.

context_blocks.text: Metric labeling combines local assignment costs with penalties for assigning far-apart labels to neighboring vertices. It captures a broad family of classification and partitioning objectives.

General algorithms give logarithmic approximation, while the square-root logarithmic scale arises in hardness. Closing the gap would identify the approximation power of this general model. Results for a uniform, line or truncated metric leave arbitrary label metrics unresolved.

why: Close a major gap for a general labeling objective linking metric geometry and approximation.
answer_criterion: Prove the stated proposition or its logical negation, with the specified quantifiers, model and guarantees. A conditional theorem settles only that conditional claim. Benchmark acceptance requires a complete proof-assistant-checked proof of the full target.
